evidence: Verg. G. 2.220: nec scabiē et salsā laedit rōbīgine ferrum
Ov. F. 6.150: frondēs laedit hiems (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “to hurt by striking, wound, injure, damage”; of frost, rust and weather as of blows.

terms.gloss: damage, a defect (in a building or a thing)
evidence: Cic. Fam. 9.15.5: sī enim nihil est in parietibus aut in tēctō vitī
Cic. Top. 15: sī aedēs corruērunt vitiumve fēcērunt (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: To become damaged, of a building: vitium facere (Cic. Top. 15); of water going bad, vitium capere (Ov. Pont. 1.5.6).

evidence: Cato Agr. 3.3: damnī nihil erit ex tempestāte
terms.comment: The damage as what it costs the owner (see loss).

phrases.latin: sī enim nihil est in parietibus aut in tēctō vitī, cētera mihi probābuntur
phrases.english: for if there’s no damage in the walls or the roof, I’ll be happy with the rest

phrases.latin: cernis ut ignāvum corrumpant ōtia corpus, ut capiant vitium, nī moveantur, aquae
phrases.english: you see how idleness spoils a lazy body, as water goes bad if it doesn’t move

phrases.latin: onerāriās, quae ad ancorās erant dēligātae, tempestās adflīctābat
phrases.english: the storm was battering the transports that were riding at anchor
